symptom: `mxcli marketplace update <id> -p app.mpr --to <version>` (and `marketplace install`) leaves the package's own metadata in the app root: `manifest.json`, `License.txt`, `SiemensMendix<Module>__<ver>__READMEOSS_<timestamp>.html` (and on BusinessEvents, `Mendix EULA.docx`) show up as untracked files. Model and mx check are fine.
cause: InstallPackageFiles copied every archive entry except project.mpr and package.xml. package.xml's `<modelerProject><files>` list is the package's declaration of its project files, and nothing read it; the publisher's metadata sits at the archive root, undeclared.
file: `cmd/mxcli/marketplace/update.go` (`declaredProjectFiles`, `isProjectFile`, `ReasonNotAProjectFile`), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_marketplace_update.go` (`reportSkippedFiles` groups them on one line); tests `cmd/mxcli/marketplace/install_declared_files_test.go`, `cmd/mxcli/cmd_marketplace_skipped_report_test.go`
insight: The arbiter was one `mx module-import` into a blank 11.12.1 app with a before/after `find`: mx wrote exactly the `<files>` entries of ExternalDatabaseConnector 6.3.0 + BusinessEvents 3.12.1 (175 + 16), no root file, and silently passed over a listed entry the archive lacks (the snowflake jar stripped from mx-modules/). That settles both 'which entries' and 'is a missing listed entry an error' without guessing. Comparing `<files>` against `unzip -Z1` on every .mpk in the repo first showed the only undeclared entries are root-level metadata — cheap, and it is what made the declared list safe to trust. The earlier relative-path test (finding 2026-09-20) used manifest.json as its 'legitimate entry' and so encoded this bug as expected behaviour; check old tests' fixtures when tightening what gets installed. Distinguish an empty `<files/>` (installs nothing) from no list (fallback: skip root-level entries only).
